column7: When a project's ticket queue outruns one seat (Kam's standing grant): launch parallel seats until it is dry. Partition by DIRECTORY, stated in both briefs with the foreseeable breach as a STOP; own worktree each. Signature classes and the QA gate still apply.

When parallel seats share one checkout and I am about to push or kill: hold the mkdir push lock from snapshot to verify (never remove another seat's lock); attribute a foreign ref only by the other seat's namespace, else STOP; kill by ancestry, never basename.

When briefing parallel seats: say near the top of EVERY brief that the seats share one inbox and a brief naming another seat is not theirs. For each shared resource (inbox, .git, process table, board, load) name how a seat tells its own from the other's.

When tapping a parallel seat: point at ITS OWN mail subject, read back at the destination (cockpit.sh say --mail). When two parallel seats conflict: that is the partition's failure; report it and re-partition, never merge through.

When writing a glob over a synced brain folder: exclude '(conflict_on_' files; a bare glob there is a defect. Never delete or rename the conflict copies, and diff one before calling it junk (it may hold a lost edit).

When a rule is withdrawn, superseded or narrowed: amend the lesson's HEADING in the same edit, not only the body. Digests carry headings only, so a retraction left in the body is still served to a cold seat as the live rule.

When running a pass/fail or there/not-there check: name the third state (the measurement did not happen) and run a positive control BEFORE wanting the answer. If the altitude cannot show 'did not happen' (job vs step, line count), go one level down.

When writing a brief or question that offers two answers ('because of this change, or already failing?'): two options teach the reader there are only two. Where a third is possible, say so: 'or tell me it is neither'.

When checking the items a ticket or list names ('are the three fixed?'): enumerate the whole set from the source (e.g. git ls-tree for ALL), do not verify the handed list. A handed list is a frame and can exclude the answer.

Before writing 'ratified', 'endorsed' or 'your reasoning is right' to an agent: open the artefact it rests on; unread, say 'received, goes to the gate, unread by me'. Ratify shapes; product claims go to the gate; a relayed fix-shape is a proposal, say so.

Before making an instrument a REQUIRED gate leg: establish it can REACH the change (grep the profile's exclusions, find the operation in the spec). A green from a leg that cannot fail is worse than no leg, because it comes with a receipt.

When a measurement kills a requirement I imposed: retract it BY NAME in the next instruction to the seat. Recording the refutation in a report is not a retraction: seats read briefs as instructions, so the dead requirement keeps executing.
When an agent refuses or contradicts something I endorsed: treat it as the system working and say so first. Never penalise it or receive it flatly; that is what would make the next catch invisible.

When a checker whose failure path restores, reverts, deletes or kills reads DIFF on a real event and no arm proves that legitimate shape passes: STOP and ask, verify read-only, do not run the remedy. Fix the checker for its NEXT use, arms written first.

When briefing a checker: put each legitimate shape through the RULE text clause by clause, in its ordinary form too (push -u, a refused or no-op push), and carry a table: shape, expected verdict, the clause that yields it.
When reading a seat's wrap mail: score and pane_close.sh in the SAME action, never 'score now, close later'. A wrapped seat with an open pane is a live agent to every pane census.

Before any 'no other agents' deadline or census-gated run: list the panes myself (tmux list-panes -t fleet:0) 10 minutes before and again at the minute; close wrapped ones, report the rest as a missed deadline. Never rely on a wrap's wake arriving.
When building or arming an unattended runner: make each INPUT it depends on a gate that refuses with the reason (e.g. the source checkout holds the develop tip), not only the pane census.

When I notice a wake that never arrived (a wrap or STATUS sat unread): write the ledger row at once with the runner log as the instrument, never 'noted, not diagnosed'. Two in one evening is a mechanism failure.

Before a question or card to Kam: list its load-bearing premises and the source of each; verify at source or write 'reported, unverified'. Urgency ('X is blocked on Y') is a premise: measure it first. If one proves false, correct it before he rules.

Before sending a negative claim ('not on', 'nothing', 'no review', 'never'): name the measurement that covers the WHOLE space; else state only what was measured ('0 formal reviews'). Measure the thing itself, not my memory of the command that made it.

Before telling anyone that X needs Kam (or that I may not do it): find the written grant or rule that decides it and quote it. Who may do what is a fact that lives in a written rule, not in my model of it.

When about to send 'you have not done X', 'no reply yet' or 'nobody picked this up': re-read the source in the SAME command that sends; compose first, verify last. A correct listing taken minutes ago is already old.

When I am about to push anything that changes a shared head (main): send the mail BEFORE the push, so no fact lives only in a pane. Batching the mail to the end of a work unit is fine for a gate, wrong for a push.

When a reproach or claim I sent proves wrong: withdraw it in the next action, naming both timestamps and exactly what was refuted, and say which parts survive (a true rule, a real gap). 'Never mind' erases the true half.

When writing a sweep that emits a list of suspect tests or sites: give it a self-test that ABORTS (a known-changed path is in, a known-unchanged path is out, the population is non-empty). State exclusions as 'by construction' with the reason.

When reporting a test disarmed by an earlier gate: say both halves (the product may be correct; the guard is now unexercised, a coverage defect). The fix is usually one line in the FIXTURE to satisfy the new gate, not a change to the policy.

When Kam answers a card with a note, not an option: the note IS the ruling and may be wider than the options. Record it verbatim by hand (the reconciler cannot parse a note) and state my reading back in the same action, naming what I treat as still his.

KS-1175's hold is lifted: build and gate its real fix. A lifted hold lifts that ONE ticket, not the class. Still Kam's: deploying it, anchoring a real record, and running KS-1250's smoke test on a live box (building and merging that script fix is not paused).

When I refute a ticket's stated cause: that kills the mechanism, not the conclusion. Before removing a blocker (a security one above all, or when removal is convenient), name the other routes checked and take one more measurement.

Before accepting a reason for ruling a ticket in or out: restate the ticket's question in one sentence and check the evidence is about THAT, not a true fact about a neighbouring question. Well-measured evidence is not relevant evidence.

When a line gates someone else's decision: never write 'works' or 'measured' for what is only strongly implied (provisioned and granted is not executed). If an agent offers a cheaper next measurement, take it before ruling.

When a fix touches a control that falls back silently (a WARN, nothing red): the fix includes making the fallback loud, not only wiring the path. A feature that cannot announce its own absence is itself a defect.

When I am about to write 'your call' or a question with options to Kam: make it a card (decision_queue.sh add: one decision, options, recommended, default) the moment it exists, on my own seat's tab; chat may only point at it. Rule it when he answers.

When Kam says he cannot see a card: ask for the board footer line or a screenshot FIRST (synced 0 = API or auth; synced >0 with need-you 0 = filter, tab or key) and measure the cause that session. HTTP 201 proves storage, never 'it is on the board'.

When decision_queue.sh refuses a card on a prior ruling: read each match; if it is a different subject, re-add with _override_prior stating the measurement. Never name another client's cards or ids in the override text.

When Kam taps a card (it arrives as chat 'Decision <id>: a'; the store is unchanged): decision_queue.sh rule <id> <key> in the same step as acting, then --delivered. If tapped_but_open.sh prints anything, rule those cards before any other step.

When a seat's QUESTION has its ANSWER verified delivered: run fleet_ack.sh answered '<subject>' in the same step (rc 3 = no match yet, re-run after the collector ticks). fleet_ack.sh list must read FLAGGED 0 at every checkpoint unless a question is open.

When I sync, copy, move or migrate: not done until every top-level and project folder is counted (files, bytes) on both sides and the table is with Kam; exit 0 is no proof. Empty here, full there is an ALARM: report first, never delete to resolve it.

When syncing or freeing space: syncs never delete (no --delete or mirror; replaced files go to a dated backup dir). Clean-up = list candidates with sizes, Kam picks, quarantine first; before any removal prove a second copy by count, not by name.

When a long copy must be interrupted: write _INCOMPLETE_COPY_<date>.txt at the destination root naming what was not copied. Before trusting a drive as complete, look for that marker; a folder that exists is not a folder that was copied.

When asked to remove empty folders: only after the copy that could refill them has finished; never inside .git, node_modules, virtualenvs, hidden tool folders or templates; record every removed path with a one-command re-create script.

When a Datasec change is READY (gate pass at the deployed head, completion check, merged through CodeQL): deploy the Composer demo or hosted HPSM-POC per runbook unasked, report after. Kam's: production, money, any human, read-only releases, MPS hosted.

When a Datasec change has a QA gate verdict at its current head plus the full verify: merge on my own GO and report after. One merge at a time, re-read main after each; CodeQL never bypassed, no alert dismissed. Re-read the grant if Kam switches accounts.

When I am about to say something waits on Kam: post it as a fleet-activity card in the same action, never a sentence; 'N items wait on you' names N cards on the board. Verify each at source first; a stale 'waiting' row is closed, not carded.

At the start of each morning: post a summary-and-plan card in the standard card shape (BLUF, options, recommended, default) with counts of what awaits Kam per project and no descriptions; those items are already cards on the board.

When a seat or the machine is idle: never wait on Kam; launch ticket lanes, as many as the code partition and load allow (Datasec order: HPSM-POC, MPS Calculator, Security Composer). A blocker is never pushed past: card it, re-raise it, escalate.

When a card for Kam has sat unanswered 48 hours: email him (Datasec seat: his datasec.com.au address); the subject names the card, the body carries its BLUF and default. Run it as a mechanism, not a habit.

When a card or brief would open any field to the public: state what the field HOLDS (the column and how the write side fills it), never just its name. A field named OrganizationId held a user id and Kam ruled on the wrong description.

When Secuura work meets a test cell pinning 'cross-company audit read refused': it now pins the opposite of Kam's rule. Name it in the next build seat's brief; never silently keep or delete it. Briefs carry his rule verbatim in RULED BY KAM.

Secuura certification verify is open to any caller, anonymous included; an anonymous call records NO billing event, signed-in calls bill as today. Public verification shows document title and issuing company name; no certifier name or user id.
